present_on_scene_date.note: Heald commanded the post until the evacuation on 15 August (his own report, Quaife App. IV).

associated_with.note: Whistler's index names the commanding officer's barracks; that the Healds lived in it in 1812 is inferred from his command, and Wau-Bun's Black Partridge enters 'the quarters of the commanding officer'.

not_in_this_household.note: The Healds' son, stillborn on 4 May 1812 (Heald's journal), died before the scene date and has no card.

persons.note: Currey says 37 in 1812; the Journal birth date makes him 36 on 14 Aug 1812. After 14 August: Wounded (thigh and right forearm per Darius Heald); taken to St Joseph, by canoe to Mackinac, paroled; Detroit, Buffalo, Pittsburgh (report 23 Oct 1812), Louisville 19 Nov 1812; major from 26 Aug 1812; disbanded 1814; St Charles Co., Missouri; died 1832.

persons.name: Cicely

present_on_scene_date.note: Helm lists 'Mrs. Heald's Negro woman' among women killed in the action; Quaife: an inmate of the fort from June 1811 until the massacre. No source takes a roll call on the afternoon of 14 August 1812; this is read from the evidence below.

persons.note: Enslaved by the Healds; the sources call her Mrs. Heald's servant or slave and give her no other name. Came from Louisville with the Healds on horseback, June 1811. Rebekah Heald's 1855 memorandum for the property claim says Kinzie had offered $600 for her, and lists 'the loss of the two slaves'. After 14 August: Killed in the battle with her infant son.
persons.review_note: review_required: Enslaved people held by the commanding officer's wife. Sources name the woman only as Cicely and the child not at all; every surviving description is by the enslavers' family (Rebekah and Darius Heald) or by Helm. Depict and caption with care, never invent a surname, age or speech; the property-claim memorandum treats them as lost property, which is evidence of their status, not a description of them.
